title: Dynamic segment-slicing for paged KV to reduce decode stalls under mixed-length workloads
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Problem: Under workloads with a mix of short and very long sequences we observe intermittent decode stalls and tail-latency spikes caused by large KV segments being loaded or compacted during active prefill waves. The current page-granularity allocation forces heavyweight evictions and full-segment moves that interfere with kernel scheduling and prefill throughput. Goal: Introduce a dynamic segment-slicing layer that allows the runtime to split oversized KV segments into slice-sized units at allocation time, enabling fine-grained eviction, background consolidation, and decode-wave-aware placement. This should reduce tail latency, improve scheduling flexibility for kernel selection (by avoiding large memory-copy slowpaths), and allow opportunistic reuse of hot subsegments across concurrent requests.
acceptance_criteria: Tail 99.9 latency for mixed-length benchmark reduced by >= 20% on our production-like rig (same model family used in benchmark-usc1)
Average decode throughput unchanged or improved (no >5% regression in median throughput)
No increase in OOM incidents in 72h soak with representative traffic; background consolidation respects SLOs and back-off signals
End-to-end tests that simulate slice boundary reuse show correctness (KV hits/misses consistent with canonical prefill semantics)
Implementation gated behind a feature flag and accompanied by telemetry: slice size histogram, slice split/merge counts, background-compaction time-series
steps: Design: define slice size heuristics (static vs. adaptive based on sequence-length distribution)
Runtime: add slice metadata to KV entries and allocation table; implement fast-path lookup by (shard, segment_id, slice_offset)
Eviction: implement slice-level LRU with tombstone coalescing for adjacent free slices
Prefill scheduling: modify prefill planner to prefer colocated hot-slices and avoid scheduling prefill that touches >N slices simultaneously
Kernel selection: expose slice-awareness hints to kernel router so large contiguous slices get memcpy-optimized kernels and scattered slices prefer gather-friendly kernels
Background: implement async consolidator that merges low-residency adjacent slices during low-load windows
Telemetry & experiments: add slice metrics, A/B feature-flag rollout, run mixed-length benchmark harness and production canary
comments: 2025-02-12 - Liam O'Connor: Spiked a prototype splitting logic in the simulator. Early results: 18% reduction in 99.9 latency for mixed job set, but fragmentation rose by 12% causing modest memory pressure. Need consolidation policy.

2025-02-18 - Ava Chen: POC integrated into local runtime. Observed decode slowpaths triggered when >3 concurrent prefill waves hit the same original segment. Proposed per-segment mutex-free slice descriptors to allow concurrent writes.
2025-02-20 - Marcus Patel (review): Concern about slice metadata overhead and cache-line amplification. Suggest packing slice descriptors and adding an epoch counter for safe concurrent reclamation.

2025-02-24 - Ava Chen: Implemented compact slice descriptor (16 bytes) and an RCU-style reclamation path. Benchmarks show descriptor overhead <2% memory but fragmentation is now manageable with consolidation.
2025-02-26 - Design review (Priya Rao): UX/observability ask - surface a per-route "slice-heatmap" in Console to troubleshoot evictions affecting latency. Added to follow-ups.
2025-02-28 - PR: github.com/redwood/realtime/compare/ENG-82419-slice-kv (draft). Key files: kv/slice_allocator.cc, scheduler/prefill_planner.cc, router/kernel_hint.cc

2025-03-01 - Load test: 48h canary at us-central-1 with feature flag ON at 10% traffic. Results: 22% reduction in 99.9 tail latency, median steady, background consolidation CPU <6% of runtime. No incidents. Moving to wider canary next week.
